newsitem.title: GERMANY: Colombia coffee growers to seek productivity gains.
newsitem.headline: Colombia coffee growers to seek productivity gains.

text.p: Colombian coffee producers will seek to raise productivity and output within a difficult economic environment, said Ricardo Avellaneda, an advisor to the Coffee Growers Federation of Colombia.
"Production costs have become too high...we're seeking higher yields, higher labour efficiency and improved farm management," he told the World Coffee Conference in Hamburg.
"There are a number of negative variables working against coffee."
Avellaneda cited peso depreciations and the focus on metals and oil exports rather than farm commodities.
Production costs of 90 cents per lb at farm level compared with 58 cents in 1989 as industrialisation had boosted labour and materials prices.
"If it stays that high, we could soon be out of the market," Avellaneda said.
But average productivity of 14 bags per hectare compared favourably with the Central American average of 12 bags.
In a study mappping out planned efficiency measures, the Growers Federation envisaged output at 13.5 million bags in the year 2000 compared with 13.05 million today.
The area would fall to 600,000 hectares from 940,000 ha at present, it estimated.
The labour force would be reduced from 700,000 to perhaps 300,000-400,000 within five years.
Productivity should be raised to 23 bags per hectare from 14 as many growers had already achieved 50 bags.
"This plan would allow us to be profitable and competitive in international markets," Avellaneda said.
